intro: 'Without parables he did not speak to them.' Forty-odd stories and images, from a seed to a wedding feast, most of them found in Matthew and Luke. Where a parable is told by more than one evangelist, every telling is listed; the first is the fullest.

items.k: Seed on the path, the rocks, the thorns and the good ground — the only parable Jesus explains word by word.
Let both grow until the harvest.
The smallest seed, the largest shrub; birds in its branches.
A little yeast hidden in three measures of flour.
A man sells everything for a field.
A merchant sells everything for one pearl.
Good fish and bad, sorted on the shore at the end of the world.
Night and day the seed grows, and the man knows not how — only in Mark.
Light is for a lampstand.

items.n: The house on rock and on sand
items.k: The end of the Sermon on the Mount: hearing and doing.
No patch of new cloth on an old garment; no new wine in old skins.
Told in Simon the Pharisee's house while a woman washes his feet: he who is forgiven more loves more.
'Which of these three was neighbour to him that fell among robbers?'
Three loaves, a closed door, and persistence.
Bigger barns, and 'this night they require thy soul of thee'.
Loins girded, lamps burning, waiting for the master to return from the wedding.

items.n: The faithful and the wicked steward
items.k: 'To whom much is given, of him much shall be required.'
One more year, and I will dig about it and dung it.

items.n: The lowest place at the feast
items.k: 'Friend, go up higher.'
The invited make excuses; the poor, the maimed, the blind and the lame fill the house. Matthew's version is a king's wedding, with a guest without a garment.

items.n: The tower and the king going to war
items.k: Count the cost before you build.
Ninety-nine left on the hills for the one.
A woman sweeps the house for one drachma and calls the neighbours.
'This my son was dead, and is come to life again' — and the elder brother outside in the dark.
Commended for his shrewdness: make friends with the mammon of iniquity.
The beggar at the gate, the bosom of Abraham, and the great gulf.
'We have done that which we ought to do.'
The widow who would not stop knocking: pray always and faint not.
'O God, be merciful to me a sinner' — and this man went home justified.
Hired at dawn and at the eleventh hour, all paid a denarius: 'Is thy eye evil, because I am good?'
One says no and goes; one says yes and does not.
The vineyard, the servants beaten, the son killed — told to the priests' faces in Holy Week.
Forgiven ten thousand talents, he strangles a man for a hundred pence. Seventy times seven.
Five wise with oil, five foolish without, and the bridegroom at midnight.
Five, two and one; the servant who buried his in the ground. Luke's version is the pounds (minas).
'As long as you did it to one of these my least brethren, you did it to me.'
'We have piped to you, and you have not danced.'
The house swept and empty, and seven spirits worse than the first.
Things new and old brought out of the storeroom: the scribe instructed in the kingdom.
When its branch is tender, summer is near.

items.n: The good shepherd and the door
items.k: John's Gospel has no parables in the Synoptic sense, but two great images: the shepherd who lays down his life, and the door of the sheep.
'Abide in me' — spoken on the night before he died.

intro: Thirty-seven miracles are recorded in the four Gospels — healings, exorcisms, the dead raised, and the works over nature. John calls his seven 'signs', and ends by saying the world could not hold the books if all were written.

items.k: The first sign, at a wedding, at his mother's word.

items.n: The nobleman's son healed at a distance
items.k: 'Go thy way, thy son liveth' — the second sign.

items.n: The demoniac in the synagogue at Capernaum
items.k: The first exorcism; the spirit knows his name.
The fever leaves her, and she serves them.
'Launch out into the deep' — and Peter falls at his knees.
'I will. Be thou made clean' — and he touches him.

items.n: The paralytic lowered through the roof
items.k: 'Thy sins are forgiven thee' first; then, 'take up thy bed'.

items.n: The man at the pool of Bethesda
items.k: Thirty-eight years; healed on the Sabbath.

items.n: The man with the withered hand
items.k: Healed on the Sabbath, in the synagogue, while they watched.
'Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof' — prayed at every Mass.
The first raising of the dead: he touches the bier.
Followed by the accusation that he casts out devils by Beelzebub.
'Peace, be still.' Who is this, that wind and sea obey him?

items.n: The Gerasene demoniac and the swine
items.k: 'My name is Legion' — and two thousand pigs into the sea.

items.n: The woman with the issue of blood
items.k: She touches the hem of his garment in the crowd.
'Talitha cumi' — little girl, arise.
'According to your faith, be it done unto you.'
'Never was the like seen in Israel.'
The only miracle in all four Gospels: five loaves, two fish, twelve baskets.
'It is I, fear not' — and Peter steps out of the boat.
'Even the dogs eat the crumbs' — a Gentile mother's wit and faith.

items.n: The deaf man with the impediment
items.k: 'Ephpheta' — be opened.
Seven loaves, seven baskets, in Gentile country.
Healed in two stages: 'I see men as it were trees, walking.'
Clay and spittle, the pool of Siloam, and a trial before the Pharisees.

items.n: The boy with the demon after the Transfiguration
items.k: 'I believe, Lord; help my unbelief.'

items.n: The coin in the fish's mouth
items.k: The Temple tax paid from a fish.
Eighteen years; loosed on the Sabbath, 'this daughter of Abraham'.
At a Pharisee's table, on the Sabbath.
Ten healed, one — a Samaritan — comes back to give thanks.
'Lazarus, come forth' — four days in the tomb.
'Son of David, have mercy on me' — he throws away his cloak and runs.
The one destructive miracle, a sign against the fruitless Temple.
The last healing, in Gethsemane, of the man who came to arrest him.
A hundred and fifty-three fish, and breakfast on the shore.
The sign of Jonah: three days, and the tomb is empty.
From the Mount of Olives, a cloud, and two men in white.

intro: Given at Sinai in fire and smoke, written by the finger of God on two tablets. The Catholic numbering follows Augustine: the first commandment includes the ban on images, and coveting is divided in two.

items.n: I am the Lord thy God: thou shalt not have strange gods before me.
items.k: Exodus 20:2–6

items.n: Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain.
items.k: Exodus 20:7

items.n: Remember that thou keep holy the sabbath day.
items.k: Exodus 20:8–11

items.n: Honour thy father and thy mother.
items.k: Exodus 20:12
Exodus 20:13
Exodus 20:14
Exodus 20:15

items.n: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
items.k: Exodus 20:16

items.n: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife.
items.k: Exodus 20:17

items.n: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's goods.
items.k: Exodus 20:17

intro: The opening of the Sermon on the Mount: eight blessings that turn the world's values upside down. Luke gives four, with four woes.

items.n: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
Blessed are the meek: for they shall possess the land.
Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are they that hunger and thirst after justice: for they shall have their fill.
Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the clean of heart: for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
Blessed are they that suffer persecution for justice' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

intro: Seven times in John Jesus says 'I am' with an image — and several times without one, echoing the name God gave Moses at the bush: 'I AM WHO AM.'

items.n: I am the bread of life.
I am the light of the world.
I am the door of the sheep.
items.k: John 10:7, 9

items.n: I am the resurrection and the life.
items.k: John 11:25

items.n: I am the way, and the truth, and the life.
items.k: John 14:6
John 15:1, 5

items.n: Before Abraham was made, I am.
items.k: John 8:58 — and they took up stones

intro: The seven sentences spoken from the cross, gathered from all four Gospels, in the traditional order.

items.n: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
items.k: Luke 23:34

items.n: Amen I say to thee, this day thou shalt be with me in paradise.
items.k: Luke 23:43

items.n: Woman, behold thy son. Behold thy mother.
My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
items.k: Matthew 27:46; Mark 15:34 — the first line of Psalm 21 (22)
John 19:28
John 19:30

items.n: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit.

sub: the numbered lists of the catechism, from Scripture
intro: The lists every Catholic child once learned by heart, each with the verse it comes from.

items.n: The seven gifts of the Holy Spirit: wisdom, understanding, counsel, fortitude, knowledge, piety, fear of the Lord.
items.k: Isaiah 11:2–3

items.n: The fruits of the Holy Spirit: charity, joy, peace, patience, benignity, goodness, longanimity, mildness, faith, modesty, continency, chastity.
items.k: Galatians 5:22–23 (twelve in the Vulgate)

items.n: The three theological virtues: faith, hope and charity — 'and the greatest of these is charity'.
items.k: 1 Corinthians 13:13

items.n: The four cardinal virtues: prudence, justice, fortitude, temperance.
items.k: Wisdom 8:7

items.n: The corporal works of mercy: feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, shelter the stranger, visit the sick, visit the imprisoned, bury the dead.
items.k: Matthew 25:35–40; Tobit 1:20–21

items.n: The two greatest commandments: love the Lord thy God with thy whole heart; love thy neighbour as thyself.
items.k: Matthew 22:37–40; Deuteronomy 6:5; Leviticus 19:18

items.n: The Golden Rule: all things whatsoever you would that men should do to you, do you also to them.
items.k: Matthew 7:12

intro: Four lists, always in three groups of four, Peter always first and Judas always last. With each: how tradition says he died.

items.k: fisherman of Bethsaida; the rock; crucified head-down in Rome under Nero, c. 64
Peter's brother, the first called; crucified on an X-shaped cross at Patras
son of Zebedee; beheaded by Herod Agrippa in Jerusalem, 44 — the first apostle to die (Acts 12)
his brother, 'the disciple whom Jesus loved'; the only one to die in old age, at Ephesus
of Bethsaida; 'come and see'; died at Hierapolis in Phrygia
'an Israelite in whom there is no guile'; flayed in Armenia
the twin, who doubted and then said 'my Lord and my God'; speared in India
the tax collector, the evangelist; martyred in Ethiopia by tradition
son of Alphaeus; thrown from the Temple and clubbed, 62
'not Iscariot'; martyred in Persia with Simon
the Cananean; sawn in two, by one tradition
the treasurer; the betrayer; hanged himself. Matthias was chosen by lot in his place (Acts 1).
